Aisha (new-hire): hi all, first-day question — running `make dev` (which runs `docker compose up`) and migrations fail with `PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server: Connection refused \nIs the server running on host \"127.0.0.1\" and accepting TCP/IP connections on port 5432?`

Aisha (new-hire): weird thing is `docker compose ps` shows the postgres service as `Up` and `docker compose logs postgres | tail` looks healthy. I also have Postgres installed on my laptop (homebrew) so `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432` connects locally.

Liam (devops): welcome Aisha :wave: this is a classic host-vs-container env mixup. Are you running the Rails process inside the docker `web` service or directly on your host?

Aisha (new-hire): I'm using `make dev` which starts everything in docker, but I ran `bundle exec rails db:migrate` from my host once when debugging, so I might've mixed envs. The repo has a `.env` with `PGHOST=127.0.0.1`.

Ravi (backend): yep if your app runs in the `web` container it should connect to the `postgres` service host (service name) not 127.0.0.1. In containers `127.0.0.1` refers to the container itself. So either change PGHOST to `postgres` for containerized runs, or change the compose service env for `web`.

Liam (devops): quick debugging commands that helped me before:
```
# see what env the container actually has
docker compose run --rm web env | grep PGHOST
# or exec into a running web container
docker compose exec web printenv PGHOST || true
```
If those print 127.0.0.1 then the container will try to talk to itself.

Nora (docs): to add: docker-compose has multiple places env can come from — `.env`, `env_file`, and `environment` in the service. Precedence is tricky: `environment` in the compose file overrides `.env`. Also your shell env can leak in if you do `docker compose run` without `--env-file` on some setups.

Ravi (backend): two common fixes:
1) Update docker-compose.override.yml (dev-only) to set `PGHOST: postgres` under the web service environment. That keeps your host `.env` untouched. Example:
```yaml
services:
  web:
    environment:
      PGHOST: postgres
```
2) Or run migrations from inside the container so they use the container env: `docker compose run --rm web bundle exec rails db:migrate`

Liam (devops): alternative if you actually want the container to connect to your host Postgres (not recommended): set `PGHOST=host.docker.internal` in the web service env (Mac/Windows) or use host networking on Linux. But again, for a dev environment we prefer the DB as another container.

Aisha (new-hire): ran `docker compose run --rm web env | grep PGHOST` and it printed `PGHOST=127.0.0.1`. Changed docker-compose.override.yml to set PGHOST=postgres, then `docker compose run --rm web bundle exec rails db:migrate` worked — migrations applied. Thank you!!

infra-bot: Welcome Aisha! You were added to #new-hires. If you need infra help ping @Liam. :robot_face:

Aisha (new-hire): small docs note: the repo `.env` is intentionally set for host-local dev (many folks run db locally), but we should document the compose override approach and `docker compose run` vs host commands so future new-hires don't confuse them. I'll open a tiny PR with the exact steps.

Nora (docs): awesome — can you include the two commands you used and the override snippet? I'll review. :memo:

Ravi (backend): also adding a troubleshooting tip to `CONTRIBUTING.md`: "If migrations are refused, run `docker compose run --rm web env | grep PGHOST` to confirm which host your app will try to connect to."

Aisha (new-hire): will do, filing the PR now :sparkles:
